  'IMPLEMENTATION. This wraps gl/accountClassification#aggregateFigures, the classifier AFS uses. The income-statement PAGE consumes reports/incomeStatementService#getIncomeStatement, and the two now AGREE band for band — turnover, other income, cost of sales, operating expenses, other expenses, gross profit, operating profit and net profit — because both band through the same exported expenseBand/revenueBand and incomeStatementConvergence.test.ts asserts every band.   'classificationCoverage is MANDATORY and present at every detail level, because every band above is chosen from account_subtype and on these books the subtypes barely exist. On one production company 100% of revenue and 97.6% of expenses sit on accounts with no classification, and its classified cost of sales is 2.4% of total costs — so its gross profit is revenue less 2.4% of what it spent. That figure is not a bug; the code did what the chart of accounts told it. READ THE COVERAGE BEFORE ACTING ON ANY BAND. reliable is false when more than 10% of either side is unclassified. tools.name: balance_sheet

description.$source:
[
  'Balance sheet as at a date, with BOTH equity figures rather than the one that always agrees.',
  'equityResidual is assets less liabilities and balances by construction — it is not evidence of anything. equityFromLedger is the sum of the POSTED equity-account balances, with nothing derived added to it.',
  'Note that totalEquity is NOT the second figure: this report computes retained earnings as revenue less expenses to the date and injects it into the equity section, so totalEquity equals equityResidual by construction and agreeing with it proves nothing.',
  'equityDifference is equityResidual − equityFromLedger, and retainedEarningsDerived is the same number named for what it is: profit that no year-end close has posted to an equity account. equityReconciles says whether it is within a cent. On two production companies the equity accounts carry R0.00 and the ENTIRE equity figure is that plug — R8,394,848.60 on one, −R34,816,224.89 on the other.',
  'compare_date adds a prior-date column with per-account priorBalance and variance, and BOTH equity figures for the prior date as well.',
  'cost_centre_id restricts every figure to one cost centre.',
  'equityReconciles is only informative BECAUSE equityFromLedger is now queried from the equity accounts rather than injected. An earlier version compared totalEquity against the residual and returned true on all three production companies — a tautology, since totalEquity equals the residual by construction. Like every self-checking identity here, a true is necessary and not sufficient: two errors that cancel satisfy it, so treat it as a precondition for inspecting the numbers rather than as a conclusion about the books.',
  'rows are the account lines of all three sections flattened, each labelled with its section. detail "summary" returns the totals and no rows.',
].join(' ')

tools.name: reconcile_subledger
tools.description: Reconciles a subledger to its general-ledger control account as at a date, and DECOMPOSES the difference into itemised reconciling items with the ids of the documents behind each one. Use it to answer "why does the AR control account disagree with what customers owe us", not merely "by how much". Returns: subledgerTotal (every open document, including ones that cannot be aged), agedTotal (what aged_debtors/aged_creditors would show), controlAccountBalance, difference, and reconcilingItems. Each item carries a bridge: "aged_to_subledger" items explain why the AGED REPORT total is not the subledger total (open disputes, which aged buckets are net of; unallocated credit notes, which never reach a bucket) and do NOT explain any GL difference; "subledger_to_control" items explain the GL difference itself (unapplied cash, postings no document claims, documents whose value never reached a control account). Those two are separate questions and adding them together produces a number that reconciles to nothing. Each bridge reports its own residual — "unexplained_difference" and "aged_unexplained_difference" — so an incomplete decomposition on either cannot be mistaken for a complete one. controlAccountBalance + the sum of the subledger_to_control items equals subledgerTotal, and agedTotal + the sum of the aged_to_subledger items equals subledgerTotal. POINT IN TIME: as_at moves BOTH sides. The subledger is reconstructed from settlement that can be dated, on the same basis as aged_debtors/aged_creditors — read the limitations on those tools, which apply here unchanged: the reconstruction will not report a settled document as outstanding, but it can UNDERSTATE a past balance where settlement carries no date (bank-match confirmation and the Sage import both write amount_paid with no dated trail). settlementFlagged lists supplier bills whose payment_matched flag says a matching process considered them settled while their balance says nothing was applied — 397 bills worth R16,151,543.00 on one production company. It is an ATTRIBUTION of part of the difference, NOT an extra reconciling item: that cash is already counted once as posting_with_no_document, so its total is deliberately outside reconcilingItems and must not be added to them. WHAT A RESIDUAL OF ZERO DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN. READ THIS BEFORE RELYING ON IT. unexplainedDifference of 0.00 is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT: it says the items sum to the difference, NOT that they are the right items. Two errors that cancel satisfy it exactly. That is not hypothetical — this endpoint reported 0.00 on every production company while wrongly counting a VAT account as an AP control account, because a reconciling item of the same amount across the same 356 documents removed it again. A phantom control account paired with a phantom offset closes the arithmetic and reads as clean books. Treat zero as a precondition for trusting the decomposition and then INSPECT THE ITEMS: check that controlAccounts holds only accounts you accept as control accounts, and that each item names documents you can follow. A non-zero residual is a mechanism this endpoint does not know about; a zero one is an invitation to look, not a conclusion. LIMITS. There is no canonical control account in this database, so EVERY candidate is returned in controlAccounts with how it was found ("subtype" = typed for the role, "posting" = subledger documents actually posted to it) and controlAccountAmbiguous is set when more than one exists; the balance is their sum. Deactivated accounts are included — is_active is a picker flag and says nothing about whether an account holds money. Only "ar" and "ap" have a document subledger to compare against; "bank", "vat", "payroll" and "inventory" return the GL control accounts with subledgerTotal null and subledgerUnavailable explaining why, rather than a difference of zero that means nothing. detail: "summary" returns totals only, "standard" (default) returns one row per reconciling item, "full" returns one row per underlying document and is paginated — call again with cursor until next_cursor is null. Follow a documentId with get_invoice, list_invoices or list_journals depending on the item type.

tools.name: general_ledger
tools.description: The general ledger for a date range: every posted line, across every account, with a running balance that INCLUDES each account’s opening balance. Use search_gl instead when you want one account and at most 200 rows; use this when you want the whole ledger, several accounts, or a filter. Filters. Account-level (account_codes, account_ids, account_types) select whole accounts and PRESERVE runningBalance. Line-level (sources, min_amount, search) select some of an account’s lines, so runningBalance is null and runningBalanceSuppressed is true — a running total over a subset is not a balance the account ever held. balanced is true only when the period is read UNFILTERED and its debits equal its credits; under any filter it is null, because debits matching credits over a subset is a coincidence and not a check. totalDebit, totalCredit, lineCount and accountCount are over the WHOLE filtered set, never just the page. openingBalances carries an entry for every account in the set, zero included. Paging: call again with cursor set and every other argument unchanged until next_cursor is null. Every line is served exactly once. COMPLETENESS: universeTotal is the UNFILTERED posted line count for the period, so rowsTotal below it means you are holding an extract and excludedTotal says how many lines your filters removed. An unfiltered call has excludedTotal 0 and rowsTotal equal to universeTotal. detail: "summary" returns totals only; "standard" (default) and "full" return lines.

tools.name: audit_trail
tools.description: WHO POSTED TO THE GENERAL LEDGER, and whether that attribution is a recorded fact or an inference. One row per GL journal entry in an entry-date range, with the actor (human | agent | system), the MCP token behind an agent posting, the posting_agent stamp, and the entry's status and amount. TWO PEOPLE, NOT ONE: user_id/user_name is who RAISED the entry, posted_by_user_id/posted_by_user_name is who COMMITTED it to the ledger. Across every production company today those are the SAME person on every single journal — there is no segregation of duties anywhere in this system, and that is a control conclusion you can state from this endpoint in one line rather than sampling for it. A draft has no poster at all. company_id, on the response rather than on each row, is whose books these are — the token decides it, so a page is never mixed. WHICH FIRM the actor was acting for is acting_company_id — the practice, on a client engagement. Read acting_company_known first: when it is false the firm was NOT RECORDED, and cross_company is null, meaning UNKNOWN. Null is not "in-house": it is the absence of a record, and every row written before migration 581 has it. Never read a null as "posted from inside this company". Filter posted_from_outside_this_company to get only postings made into these books by someone acting for a DIFFERENT recorded company — the first question a client's auditor asks of a practice engagement. Rows with no recorded firm can never satisfy it, so that filter under-reports while the write side is still being built. READ actor_provenance ON EVERY ROW. "recorded" means the write itself stored the actor. "derived" means it was inferred from the posting_agent stamp because the row predates that column, and the inference is ASYMMETRIC: an "mcp:" stamp does prove an agent, but a "human:" one proves only "not stamped as an agent" — journal creation falls back to a human stamp whenever a caller omits the posting metadata, so an unknown number of agent postings sit under derived human. actor_caveat spells this out per row. Never report a derived human as a person having typed the entry. AND A RECORDED HUMAN IS A WEAKER CLAIM THAN IT LOOKS: nothing in IsaFlow writes actor_type "human" by default, so a recorded human means some caller explicitly asserted one — it is not produced by a person using the UI, and the absence of an agent stamp is not proof of a person. An agent posting is provable; a human posting is not. Say "not recorded as an agent", never "typed by a person". The attribution block totals recorded vs derived across the whole filtered range (not just the page), which is the honest measure of how much of this ledger can be relied on. DOES NOT COVER: non-ledger changes. Editing a customer, changing a bank rule or logging in leaves no journal and does not appear here; the separate audit_log table holds field-level change history and is effectively unused (5 rows across production). Nor does it cover documents that have not posted — an unapproved draft invoice or credit note has no journal yet. entity_id needs an entity_type saying which link to match: "journal" = the entry's own id, "source_record" = the bank transaction / invoice / credit note it was raised from, "source_document" = the captured document. universeTotal is present unless an actor_type, token_jti or acting_company_id filter is applied — with one the result is a selection, not a census, and completeness is not a claim being made. tools.description: Whether a company's imported bank history can account for itself, per bank account. tools.name: asset_register
tools.description: Reconcile the fixed asset register to the general ledger as at a date, and report the gap. This is the assurance call: it returns the register carrying amount, the GL carrying amount, and the difference between them, with the individual GL accounts behind each side. The GL side is selected by account SUBTYPE — fixed_assets for cost, accumulated_depreciation for the contra — never by account name, because choosing a bucket by name is how two default_expense accounts became cost of sales and overstated gross profit by R562,428. It applies NO is_active filter: a deactivated account with a balance is still on the balance sheet. READ THE ACCOUNT LIST, NOT JUST THE TOTAL. On these books every account subtyped fixed_assets that carries a balance is an intercompany loan or investment account, so the total presents millions of rands of loans as property, plant and equipment. The list is what makes that visible. reconciled is true only when the difference is exactly zero. A non-zero difference does not tell you which side is wrong — a register that was never posted to the GL, depreciation journalised against no asset, or an account with the wrong subtype all produce one. It reports the gap; it does not repair it, does not run depreciation, and does not post anything.

tools.name: reconcile_fixed_assets
tools.description: Reconciles the fixed asset register to the general ledger as at a date and DECOMPOSES the difference into itemised reconciling items, each carrying the id of the asset or the GL account behind it. Use it to answer "why does the balance sheet disagree with the asset register", not merely "by how much". asset_register reports the same two totals without the items. Returns registerNetBookValue (cost less accumulated depreciation from the assets table), glNetBookValue (posted balances of every account subtyped fixed_assets or accumulated_depreciation), difference = register less GL, and one row per asset and per account. Each row contributes its own amount to the difference. THE TWO SIDES ARE INDEPENDENTLY DERIVED: the register comes from the assets table and the ledger from posted journal lines, so the difference can genuinely be non-zero. WHAT A ZERO DIFFERENCE DOES AND DOES NOT PROVE. READ THIS BEFORE RELYING ON IT. It is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. The items sum to the difference by construction — every asset and every account is reported — so a zero says the two totals happen to agree, NOT that the register and the ledger describe the same assets. Two errors that cancel satisfy it exactly. Treat a zero as an invitation to INSPECT THE ITEMS, never as a conclusion about the accounts. WHAT TO INSPECT. normal_balance_violated marks a cost account carrying a CREDIT balance, or an accumulated-depreciation account carrying a DEBIT one: the sign is opposite to what the subtype implies, so the account is unlikely to be property, plant and equipment. On these books that flag catches millions of rands of loan and investment accounts subtyped fixed_assets, which any single total would present as PPE. The tool REPORTS them; it does not reclassify anything and does not change the chart of accounts. register_linkage_available is false when NO asset and no asset category in the company records a GL account — the state of every production company today. While it is false NO part of the ledger can be attributed to a specific asset, by any means, because the data that would make the link does not exist. Items therefore carry no per-asset attribution field: there is nothing to compute one from, and a field that could only ever hold one value would read as a check that had run. ACCOUNT SELECTION is by SUBTYPE, never by account name — choosing a bucket by name is how two default_expense accounts became cost of sales and overstated gross profit by R562,428. There is NO is_active filter: a deactivated account with a live balance is still on the balance sheet. An asset disposed on or before as_at is not carrying amount; it appears in excludedRows with the book value it was still carrying, never silently dropped — as disposed_before_as_at when a journal posted for it, and as disposal_not_posted_to_ledger when none did. READ unposted_disposals. A disposal the register recorded and the ledger never heard about is the one register-versus-ledger break that can NEVER move the difference: the asset is out of the register carrying amount and the journal is absent from the ledger, so both sides are zero and the arithmetic closes over a real loss. unposted_disposal_gain_loss is profit or loss that never reached the income statement and unposted_disposal_book_value is cost less depreciation never removed from the balance sheet. Production holds exactly one disposal and it is in this list: Brightsphere COMP-0001, sold 2026-04-12 for R8,000 against a R15,000 book value, a R7,000 loss with no journal. disposal_record_count above 1 means the asset carries more than one disposal record: the LATEST is reported, and where an older one posted while the newest did not the amounts shown describe the older event — go and look at that asset rather than trusting the figures on it. It cannot post on ANY tenant — posting a disposal resolves the system account role disposal_profit_loss and no company has an account carrying that subtype, so the posting throws before it writes. Fixing that is a chart-of-accounts change; this tool reports it and changes nothing. READ disclosures BEFORE TRUSTING A ZERO. Accounts are selected by SUBTYPE, so an account typed asset that carries NONE is in neither side of this reconciliation — and because the items and the totals come from the same subtype-filtered query, its balance could never make the difference non-zero. Every such account is listed in disclosures with its id and balance, and unsubtyped_account_balance totals them: Velocity Fibre has 58 holding R32,747,547.38, including PPE cost and accumulated-depreciation accounts. They are DISCLOSURES and not excludedRows on purpose — an exclusion is a row that belonged to this report and was withheld, while these were never in its universe, and most of them are debtors or cash rather than fixed assets. This tool cannot tell which is which, because nothing here is inferred from an account NAME. A difference of zero alongside a non-zero unsubtyped_account_balance is not a reconciliation; set the subtype with update_gl_account and re-run. WHAT CHECKS WHICH NUMBER. difference, itemsTotal and unexplainedDifference are guarded by an arithmetic you can verify: the items sum to the difference. The three figures reported BESIDE them — unsubtyped_account_balance, unposted_disposal_gain_loss and unposted_disposal_book_value — sit outside that identity because the facts they carry genuinely do not belong inside it, and unexplainedDifference of 0.00 tells you NOTHING about whether any of them is right. Each is instead checked against THE ROWS THIS RESPONSE CARRIES, which catches a capped list or a duplicated row, and figure_guards reports the OUTCOME of that check rather than a promise of it: "enumerated" means the comparison ran and agreed, "unguarded" means the rows were not emitted and nothing checked the figure. disclosureFault appears when a check ran and disagreed. NO check can test the query that found the rows, so a disclosure or a disposal the predicate never matched is invisible to every number here. This report makes NO completeness claim (universeTotal is absent) because its rows are PRODUCED by the reconciliation rather than selected from a pool; a universe here could only be synthesized from the numbers it would be checked against, and a claim that cannot fail is worse than none. detail: "summary" returns the totals only, "standard" (default) returns one row per reconciling item, "full" returns one row per journal entry posted to the asset-section accounts — capped at 50 entries per account, most recent first — and is paginated; call again with cursor until next_cursor is null. Follow a journal_entry_id with list_journals or audit_trail, and an asset_id with list_fixed_assets. It reports the gap; it does not repair it, does not run depreciation and posts nothing.

tools.name: run_depreciation
tools.description: Runs the monthly depreciation for every eligible fixed asset in one period, writing the per-asset result to the fixed asset subledger and posting DR Depreciation Expense / CR Accumulated Depreciation to the general ledger. period_date is the LAST DAY of the period being depreciated (YYYY-MM-DD) and defaults to the last day of the current month. It decides the journal date, the journal entry number (DEP-<asset number>-YYYY-MM) and the subledger period, so a run for an earlier month posts into THAT month. ALWAYS CALL IT WITH dry_run: true FIRST. The dry run returns the journals that would post, in full, with the account codes and the amounts on both legs, and the assets that would be skipped with the reason for each. It writes nothing and does not consume the idempotency key. dry_run defaults to FALSE: a call without it POSTS. It refuses BEFORE writing anything when no fiscal period covers period_date, when that period is closed or locked, or when no asset would post. Those are different refusals because the remedies differ — create the fiscal year, re-open the period, or look at why every asset was skipped. An asset is skipped, not failed, when it is not in service (disposed, retired), has no purchase price, is marked below the capitalisation threshold, has no useful life on itself or its category, or already has an unreversed journal for this period. Re-running a period is therefore safe: every asset already posted is skipped by entry number. READ glFailed ON THE REPLY. It counts assets whose subledger row and journal were rolled back together as a unit while the rest of the run committed. A success with glFailed above zero is a PARTIAL run and accumulated depreciation is understated by those assets until the cause is fixed and the period re-run. It depreciates on the ACCOUNTING (IAS 16) policy only in the general ledger; the SARS wear-and-tear figure is computed and stored in the subledger but is not journalised. It does not create assets, does not dispose of them, and does not reclassify any account. Call reconcile_fixed_assets afterwards to check the register against the ledger — on these books they do not agree, and a depreciation run does not make them.

tools.name: stock_valuation
tools.description: Quantity on hand and value per product as at a date, derived from stock movements: inbound movements add, everything else subtracts, and value is the cost recorded ON each movement. READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE TOTAL. Every stock movement in these books is a purchase carrying total_cost 0.00, so stock has been received and never valued — the report returns a real quantity against a zero value and flags each such product with unvalued: true rather than presenting R0 as a valuation somebody computed. It reads the products/stock_movements model, which is the one that holds data. The items and stock_items catalogues are separate and empty; list_items shows the first of those. stock_movements and stock_levels have NO company_id column of their own, so this report is tenant-scoped by joining products. Movements whose product carries no company_id belong to no tenant and are NOT attributed to you. Their EXISTENCE is disclosed in excludedRows as product_has_no_company; their number and value are withheld on purpose, because that query cannot be scoped to you and any figure it returned would be computed from rows that may belong to other tenants. Stocktake movements record an absolute quantity rather than a change and are excluded from quantity on hand as stocktake_count_not_a_delta. universeTotal counts YOUR products; neither disclosure inflates it. It is not a stock ledger and does not show individual movements, does not apply FIFO, weighted-average or any other costing method beyond the cost written on each movement, and is not reconciled to any GL inventory account.

tools.name: supplier_statement
tools.description: A running-balance statement of account for one supplier: every bill, payment and supplier credit note dated on or before as_at, in date order, with what we owe after each. The mirror of customer_statement, and it runs the OTHER WAY — a bill credits the balance (we owe more), a payment debits it (we owe less), and a positive closing balance means we owe the supplier. Credit notes count whether they are approved or already applied. This is OUR ledger of the supplier. It is not the reconciliation of a statement the supplier sent us — that is supplier_statement_reconciliations in the app, and this tool does not read it. detail: "summary" returns the totals with no rows.

tools.name: job_cost_report
tools.description: Logged effort and its value across EVERY time-entry status, grouped by practice client, job category or work item: hours, value and entry count in each status, plus the unbilled total. READ THIS INSTEAD OF wip_report IF YOU WANT TO KNOW WHAT IS OWED. wip_report counts only APPROVED, billable, unbilled time — the correct definition of work in progress and a badly incomplete picture of unbilled effort. tools.name: budget_variance
tools.description: Budget against actual for every revenue and expense account over a date range: the budgeted amount for the months in the range, the posted movement, and the variance between them. READ THE EXCLUSIONS BEFORE THE ROWS. Only accounts that carry a budget appear in rows. An account with real spend and no budget cannot produce a variance, so it appears in excludedRows with reason no_budget_set and its actual value — and on a company where nobody has ever set a budget, rows is EMPTY and looks identical to a company that is perfectly on plan. unbudgeted_movement totals what is sitting outside any budget. The actual is posted journal-line movement per account, signed so revenue and expense are both positive when larger: the same figure the trial balance shows. It is deliberately NOT the income statement, and DO NOT "improve" it into one — no cost-of-sales bucketing, no other-income or finance-cost layer, no tax. incomeStatementService has open defects in exactly the classification layer a variance would inherit, and a variance computed against a net profit already known to be wrong is worse than no variance, because it wears the authority of a reconciliation. The raw per-account aggregate borrows none of it. Draft journals are excluded. Variance is signed so positive is favourable: revenue actual less budget, expense budget less actual. variance_pct is a percentage of budget, and is reported as 0 where there is no budget to be a percentage of. Budgets are stored per calendar month and matched to the fiscal year given by the YEAR OF period_start. Note the split this system carries: all 13 companies DECLARE companies.financial_year_start = 3, while every fiscal_periods row actually starts 01-01 — so for the data as it stands the year of period_start is the right key, but the declaration disagrees with it. fiscal_year and months_covered are returned so the match can be re-derived rather than assumed. detail: "summary" returns totals with no rows; "standard" and "full" return the account lines.

tools.name: propose_reclassification

description.$source:
[
  'Preview moving posted amounts from one GL account to another. Writes NOTHING.',
  'HOW A RECLASSIFICATION IS DONE HERE: it posts a NEW journal — a contra on the source account and the same amount re-applied to the target, one pair per source line — and leaves the original posted lines exactly as they are. It never rewrites gl_journal_lines. That is what keeps a trial balance somebody already signed reproducible, keeps the original classification visible to an auditor, and makes the batch undoable through reverse_journal_entry.',
  'RETURNS: every journal that would post in full; the profit and loss before and after, each aggregated independently over the ledger rather than one derived from the other; the source and target account movement; gross and net moved, stated separately because an account used for clearing can show R31.6m gross against R659k net and a net-only reading would call that harmless (movement.grossMoved and movement.netMoved are raw DEBIT-POSITIVE ledger movement; account_movement is normal-balance signed, so a credit-side move shows a negative netMoved); every line that would be skipped with a machine-stable reason; and the source journal entry ids behind all of it.',
  'READ THE WARNINGS BEFORE ACTING. no_profit_and_loss_effect means every band is identical before and after, so the move changes no reported figure at all and only merges two account names — which is what happens when both accounts already report in the same band (an expense with no subtype and one subtyped default_expense both land in operating expenses). subtype_remedy_available means the source account is simply missing an account_subtype: setting it with update_gl_account achieves the same reporting goal and MOVES NOTHING, whereas this move merges the source account into the target and no report can tell them apart afterwards. On real books most unclassified accounts are correctly named and correctly loaded — they only lack a subtype — and moving them destroys the split between, say, direct material, sub-contractors and wayleave. collapses_named_accounts means the target already carries value from elsewhere.',
  'PERIODS: with no posting_date each journal is dated at its own source line, so the period that incurred the cost keeps it and nothing crosses periods — but every line whose own period is CLOSED is skipped (source_period_closed), because a closed period cannot be posted into. Pass posting_date to date the whole batch in an open period instead; nothing is then skipped for a closed source period, and the charge moves between periods.',
  `LIMITS: at most ${MAX_RECLASS_LINES} source lines per call — narrow with from/to and run several batches rather than have a batch truncate. Draft journals are not candidates; only posted lines are. Lines on a reversed entry, lines an earlier live batch already moved, and the contra legs of an earlier reclassification are skipped. Post it with post_reclassification_batch.`,
].join(' ')

tools.name: allocate_bank_transaction
tools.description: Allocate one bank transaction to a GL account (optionally matching a supplier or customer invoice). Identify the transaction by transaction_id OR by bank_reference — the reference printed on the statement — so you can allocate straight from a statement without fetching ids first (optionally narrowed by bank_account_id). POSTS a journal entry. Every allocation is attributed to the agent and can be undone with reverse_bank_allocation. DIRECTION FOLLOWS THE SIGN: a money-out line against a supplier is a payment (DR Accounts Payable / CR Bank) and a money-IN line is a supplier refund (DR Bank / CR Accounts Payable); a money-in line against a customer is a receipt and a money-out line is a customer refund. A refund is NOT applied to an invoice — name no invoice_id for one. An invoice_id whose direction contradicts the line is REFUSED, never guessed. A vat_code of standard is REFUSED on accounts where no supply can arise (salaries and statutory deductions, taxes and penalties, distributions, depreciation, donations, and exempt financial services such as interest, loans and share investments) and on entertainment accounts where input tax is denied — the line still posts, gross, and the response carries vat_coerced saying what was changed and why. description.$source:
[
  'Move posted amounts from one GL account to another, as one reversible batch. RUN propose_reclassification FIRST, or call this with dry_run: true — it returns exactly what would post and writes nothing.',
  'HOW IT WORKS: it POSTS A NEW JOURNAL — a contra on the source account and the same amount re-applied to the target, one pair per source line — and leaves every original posted line untouched. Nothing is edited or deleted. Each journal is a normal posted entry, so the batch is undone with reverse_journal_entry on the ids returned, and both the original and the correction stay in the audit trail.',
  'THE CAVEAT THAT MATTERS MOST. If the source account is missing only an account_subtype, this is probably the WRONG remedy: setting the subtype with update_gl_account gets it into the classified bands of every report and moves nothing, while this merges the source account into the target permanently — after it, no report can tell the two apart. On real books most unclassified accounts are correctly named and correctly loaded, and moving them collapses distinct costs (direct material, sub-contractors, wayleave) into one line. The response warns with subtype_remedy_available and collapses_named_accounts when either applies; read them.',
  'PERIODS: with no posting_date each journal is dated at its own source line, so nothing crosses periods — and any line whose own fiscal period is CLOSED is skipped, because a closed period cannot be posted into. Pass posting_date to post the whole batch on one open day instead; the closed month then keeps its original classification and this period carries the correction.',
  `SKIPS versus FAILURES: a line the data will not let you move — closed period, no fiscal period, a reversed entry, already moved by an earlier batch, the contra leg of one — is SKIPPED with a reason and does not cost the rest. Anything else fails the WHOLE batch and nothing is posted. At most ${MAX_RECLASS_LINES} source lines per call; narrow with from/to rather than have a batch truncate. A call with nothing left to move posts nothing and opens no batch.`,
].join(' ')

tools.name: import_bank_statement
tools.description: Import a bank statement (OFX, CSV, QIF or MT940) into a bank account. A statement reference is stored WHERE THE FORMAT CARRIES ONE — the generic and ABSA header CSV layouts (a Reference column), FNB CSV, OFX, QIF and MT940 — and is then what bank_reference resolves against in allocate_bank_transaction and reverse_bank_allocation. The Standard Bank, Capitec and Nedbank CSV layouts and the legacy positional ABSA layout carry no reference column at all, so rows imported from those resolve by transaction_id only. Transactions already present are skipped by a (date, amount, description, balance) content hash — the reference is NOT part of it, so two same-day rows with the same amount, description and balance still collapse into one even when their references differ, so re-sending the same statement is safe. Note the flip side: two genuinely separate transactions on the same day with the same amount and description hash alike, and the second will be skipped as a duplicate — reconcile the closing balance after importing rather than trusting the row count. Creates transactions only: it posts no journals and does not touch transactions it did not create. Allocate afterwards with allocate_bank_transaction. Use dry_run to see what would land before writing.

tools.name: merge_gl_accounts

description.$source:
[
  'Merge one GL account into another: every journal line on the source is repointed to the target,',
  'the source\'s child accounts are moved onto the target with their levels shifted, and the source',
  'is DEACTIVATED carrying zero. Nothing is deleted and no journal is posted — a repoint changes no',
  'debit and no credit, only which account carries it, so the company trial balance is identical',
  'afterwards. Per-account balances, comparatives and any report grouped by account DO change, for',
  'every period the moved lines touch.',
  'Built for a chart that carries two control accounts for one role — a Sage-imported account',
  'holding the old population beside the one the write path actually posts to. There is no',
  'canonical control account in this schema and the codes differ per company, so this tool takes',
  'both accounts by id and forms no opinion about which is canonical.',
  'RUN dry_run FIRST and read it. It returns both accounts\' figures derived by separate queries,',
  'the trial balance either side of the move, the journal entries as ids you can open, every row',
  'that would not move with a reason code, the child accounts that would be reparented, and what',
  'breaks if the proposal is wrong. It writes nothing.',
  'REFUSES: the same account twice; two different account_types; a target sitting below the source',
  'in the chart (a cycle); a SYSTEM account as the source, because auto-posting resolves those by',
  'subtype and deactivating one leaves the role unclaimed; a bank-subtype source that bank',
  'transactions still reference; and a source any configuration row still names (bank rules, AFS',
  'mappings, asset categories, products — the check is driven by the foreign-key catalogue, so it',
  'covers tables added after this tool was written).',
  'SKIPS BLOCK THE MERGE: a posted line in a closed fiscal period, or a posted line with no fiscal',
  'period at all, is reported with its amount and the whole merge refuses. A control-account merge',
  'that leaves part of its balance behind is worse than one that does not run.',
  'ALSO REFUSES a merge that crosses a REPORTING CLASS: vat (subtypes vat_input, vat_output, tax —',
  'what the VAT201 selects on) and bank (what the banking screens reach statement rows through)',
  'are each their own class, and everything else including NULL is ordinary. Crossing that',
  'boundary puts money that is not tax onto a SARS return in one direction and drops it off in the',
  'other, with the trial balance identical either way. Same-class merges are allowed, so the two',
  'control-account cases this tool was built for (NULL to receivable, NULL to payable) pass.',
  'Does NOT cover: configuration rows (repoint them yourself first) — and note that the',
  'configuration sweep reads foreign keys, so a reference held BY ACCOUNT CODE rather than by id',
  'is invisible to it. group_accounts.account_code is the known case: the consolidation chart',
  'resolves by code, the source keeps its code after the merge, so the group mapping goes on',
  'resolving to an account that now carries zero while the money joins the target\'s',
  'consolidation line. Check it by hand before merging an account that is in a group.',
  'It also does not rename or renumber the chart, and never merges across companies.',
  'CONCURRENCY: the live call locks both accounts for the rest of the request. If another request '
  + 'holds one, this waits 5 seconds and then refuses with a message saying to retry — that one is '
  + 'safe to re-issue with the same idempotency_key, because nothing was written. One failure mode '
  + 'is NOT specific: if the ledger changes between the preview and the write (a journal posted, a '
  + 'period closed), the merge aborts having written nothing, but reaches you as a generic failure '
  + 'rather than a named one. Re-run with dry_run to see what moved.',
].join(' ')

tools.name: post_payroll_journal
tools.description: Post the general-ledger journal for an APPROVED payroll run: debit labour cost with gross pay plus the employer UIF and SDL the company owes on top of it, and credit PAYE payable, UIF payable (both halves), SDL payable, any voluntary deductions, and net pay. This is the entry that is missing from these books. Today net pay alone is coded to Salaries & Wages, so employment cost is understated by every employer contribution and no PAYE, UIF or SDL liability is ever raised. ALWAYS call it with dry_run: true first. The preview returns the complete journal — every line, both totals, the fiscal period the date falls in, and the run totals it was derived from — and it applies every check the live call applies: the run must be approved, it must not already carry a journal, the five required GL accounts (5200 labour, 2140 PAYE, 2150 UIF, 2160 SDL, 1110 bank) must exist, and account 2175 must exist if there are voluntary deductions. If any of those fails, BOTH the preview and the live call refuse and name the reason. It reports rather than repairs. An advisory of inactive_target_account means the journal posts into deactivated accounts — is_active is only a picker flag, so the money does land there, but no one can select those accounts in the UI and any report that filters on is_active will drop the balance. It does not activate them. It also does not calculate or approve the run, does not pay anyone, and does not file an EMP201. A run with ETI will report an unbalanced blocker: ETI is currently subtracted from the labour debit and credited nowhere, so the journal will not balance and cannot post until that is corrected by a human. Reverse a posted payroll journal in the app; this tool will refuse a run that already has one rather than post a second.

tools.name: reverse_journal_entry
tools.description: Reverse a POSTED journal entry by posting a contra entry that offsets it line for line. The original KEEPS status "posted" and is marked reversed in metadata, so the pair nets to zero in every report rather than the account swinging to the negative of the original. Override with reversal_date, which must be a real YYYY-MM-DD day, must not fall before the entry being reversed, and must land in a fiscal period that EXISTS and is open. Refuses an entry that is a draft, already reversed, or has no lines. Does NOT cover: bank allocations (reverse_bank_allocation, or reverse_allocations for a date range) — reversing their journal directly would leave the bank transaction still marked allocated and pointing at an entry that has been undone. It also does not delete anything: both entries stay in the ledger, which is the point. Run with dry_run first: it reports the contra lines that would post and writes nothing.

tools.name: settle_by_contra

description.$source:
'Settle a customer invoice or a supplier bill against another GL account — a loan, '
    + 'intercompany or director\'s account — WITHOUT any cash moving. Use it when the debt was '
    + 'netted off rather than paid, which is otherwise only representable as a bank payment that '
    + 'never happened. '
    + 'subledger "ar" posts DR <contra account> / CR Accounts Receivable and reduces that '
    + "invoice's outstanding balance. subledger \"ap\" posts DR Accounts Payable / CR <contra "
    + "account> and reduces that bill's. Either way a payment document is created with "
    + 'payment_method "contra", so the settlement is afterwards distinguishable from a real bank '
    + 'movement. '
    + 'THE CONTRA ACCOUNT MUST BE A BALANCE-SHEET ACCOUNT — a loan, an intercompany or a '
    + "director's account (type asset, liability or equity). Netting a debt against an EXPENSE or "
    + 'REVENUE account is a WRITE-OFF, not a contra, and is refused naming write_off '
    + '(POST /api/accounting/write-offs), which has its own treatment. The side is decided from '
    + "the account's type and subtype, never from its name or code. "
    + 'Also REFUSES a contra account that is a bank account (that is the phantom payment this '
    + "exists to avoid), the subledger's own control account (it nets to nothing and settles the "
    + 'document against itself), a parent header account (the balance sheet excludes headers, so '
    + 'the posting would be invisible), a deactivated one, or one whose account_type and '
    + 'account_subtype are not a valid pairing (it cannot be classified, and this will not guess '
    + '— fix it with update_gl_account). Also refuses an amount above the document\'s outstanding '
    + 'balance, and a cancelled or draft document. ' 
    + 'Partial settlement is allowed — the remainder stays outstanding. '
    + 'Does NOT cover: a real bank payment (apply_receipt_to_invoice / '
    + 'apply_payment_to_supplier_invoice), a credit note that reduces what is owed for a '
    + 'commercial reason (create_credit_note), or writing a debt off to bad debts, which is a '
    + 'policy decision rather than a settlement. '
    + 'Run with dry_run first: it reports the journal that would post and writes nothing.'

tools.name: close_fiscal_period
tools.description: Close a fiscal period so nothing further can post into it. REFUSES on any failing readiness check and names every one of them with its reason — unreconciled banks, unposted draft journals, an AR or AP subledger that does not tie to its control account, an unbalanced trial balance, or a POSTED journal that belongs to no fiscal period at all — that last one is invisible to every period report while sitting in the ledger, so no close can honestly assert completeness over it. This is stricter than the app: the Month-End Workbench shows the same checks to a person who may close over them. A check that could not be COMPUTED also blocks — "the AP tie could not be checked" is exactly the state in which closing unattended is unsafe. Warnings (a period with no VAT return, uncleared opening-balance equity) do NOT block and come back in `warnings`. Also refuses a period that is locked, already closed, or has an open period before it. Run period_close_checklist or dry_run first: a dry run applies every one of these guards and writes nothing. tools.name: perform_bank_reconciliation
tools.description: Start a bank reconciliation for one account at a statement date and balance, claim every unreconciled imported transaction into it, auto-match those transactions to posted GL journal lines, and report the reconciled balance and the outstanding difference. Auto-matching only applies matches it scores at 0.9 confidence or better; anything weaker is returned as a candidate for a person and is NOT applied. It does NOT create journals: a transaction with nothing in the GL to match stays unmatched — allocate it with allocate_bank_transaction and reconcile again. complete defaults to false. With complete: true the session is completed ONLY when the difference is exactly zero AND at least one transaction was matched — an empty session balances trivially, because a reconciliation starts at the GL balance, and completing one proves nothing (production holds exactly such a reconciliation). When either condition fails the call still SUCCEEDS, reports completed: false with the difference, and leaves the session in progress so the matches are not thrown away — cancel_bank_reconciliation releases it if you want to start over. Refuses if a reconciliation is already in progress on the account. dry_run reports the GL balance at the statement date, the difference against the statement balance you supplied, and how many transactions would be claimed — and writes nothing. Requires the write:post permission.

tools.name: lock_vat_period
tools.description: Records that a VAT period has been filed and stops it being changed. Stores the return that was filed — output tax, input tax, net VAT — together with the posted_through those figures were computed at, so that a later disagreement between the filed return and the ledger can be told apart from an arithmetic error. WHY YOU NEED IT: nothing else stops a journal being posted into a period that has already been filed. One live ledger accepts a 2022 posting made today, and the return submitted for 2022 no longer agrees with the ledger it came from, with nothing recording that it ever did. RUN dry_run FIRST. The dry run runs every guard the live call runs — the period must not run backwards, must not already be locked, and its 15% check is reported — and writes nothing. It REFUSES to lock a period whose rateCheck.ties is false unless you pass force:true, because a return that fails SARS's own check is not one to freeze; fix it or record explicitly that you are filing it as it stands. IDEMPOTENT BY THE PERIOD ITSELF: locking a period that is already locked returns the EXISTING lock and does not overwrite its figures, so a retry can never rewrite what was filed. LIMITS: the lock is a record that posting paths read, not a database trigger. It does not unlock — that is deliberate; a lock you can lift with one call is not a control.
